reasoning: The PKGBUILD downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub releases with BLAKE2 checksums pinned. All other files (.SRCINFO, REUSE.toml, subtitleedit.desktop, license files) are standard metadata or legal text with no executable content. The disagreement was caused entirely by API failures (HTTP 400) in the qwen model, not by any security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no issues.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit .SRCINFO, REUSE.toml, and subtitleedit.desktop, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model reviewed the same files successfully and found them safe. This is a tool infrastructure failure, not a substantive disagreement about security.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit 3 files (.SRCINFO, REUSE.toml, subtitleedit.desktop) due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API failures should not produce inconclusive verdicts when the files in question are non-executable metadata (license files, .desktop entries, .SRCINFO). The tool should distinguish between 'could not review due to error' and 'reviewed and found concerns'.
Implement retry logic or fallback models when primary model encounters transient API errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent unnecessary escalations.
When one model fails due to infrastructure errors and another succeeds on the same files, the successful review should be weighted heavily if the files are low-risk (non-executable metadata).
